why: The r/androidgaming defending-and-repairing item mixes a called defence against overwrites with routine watching and repair, and the two gates overlap unless the called fight is weighed against the fixing leading.

why.T3-009: The codes mark the finished Android logo as achieved to celebrate ('Go us!'), with a final image and its near-perfect finish; rather than T3-026 (announcing the mark up while work goes on) or T3-073 (a plain account), the point is the celebratory wrap-up of the outcome, with announcing/saving/recounting as subordinate markers.

why.T3-044: Both codes have outsiders saying the sub's r/place logo brought them into Android Gaming, i.e. the room's mark recruiting canvas visitors; not the room's own members finding a mark already placed (T3-082).

why.T3-002: C1142490, C0690514, C1188749 and C0189906 call the room's members to come and place for Okami art (make, finish, at a spot); the expansion ideas (C0237908, C0642927) are further calls inside the same recruiting practice, not a mark merely proposed (T3-033) or a chosen design worked out (T3-004).

why.T3-057: The exchange carries the Okami pixel-art making into a proposed Minecraft server with an Okami resource pack, i.e. the design remade in another medium; not sending pixels to another room's canvas work (T3-011) or joining an outside group's canvas build (T3-137).

why.T3-084: C0997587 and C0029483 pursue other rooms' hands/cooperation to help defend the droid — a room asking another canvas room for help (T3-084), not a standing alliance (T3-150) or a fight ended (T3-149).
why.T3-153: C0671586 and C0326836 have members joining/asking into the neighbour's sub and Discord to meet them and talk, which is meeting other rooms in chat rather than asking for help.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-084 carries the requests to other rooms for hands/cooperation but cannot carry the practice of joining the neighbouring room's sub and Discord to meet them and talk terms.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0671586 (joined their sub and Discord) and C0326836 (asked for a Discord invite) are members meeting another room in its chat, exactly T3-153's gate, with no help-request content.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-153; dropping it loses the venue of the talks, but the room's pursuit of outside hands still stands on T3-084.

why.T3-068: C1149038 turns r/trees' label into r/bees and their pineapple into a bee hive — another room's art converted into the room's own sign; not destroying it (T3-006), taking its space (T3-061) or adopting it unchanged (T3-175).

why.T3-004: The codes settle and correct the logo/controller's look (grey gamepad, an altered controller, accepted button colours) — the mark's design worked out (T3-004), not repair of vandalised pixels (T3-021) nor sharing a finished template (T3-070).

why.T3-017: The exchange is about an Android game and a first-impressions video — the sub's usual subject and media — so it is ordinary sub talk carried on; the r/place welcome (C1217510) is only the occasion, not a canvas act.

why.T3-005: C1179909 (PROTECT THE ROBOT), C0956887 (fighting to protect all day) and C0609047 (defend it) answer an ongoing attack with alarms and holding the line — a fight called, T3-005.
why.T3-021: C0924159 (trying to fix), C1508512 (fixed it, clean the eyes) and C0147484 (refresh before placing) are the routine watching and repair of the work, T3-021.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-005 carries the called defence against overwrites but not the sustained hand repair and watch routine (fixing lettering, cleaning eyes, refreshing) that keeps the logo intact between attacks.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0924159, C1508512 and C0147484 are fixing changed pixels and troubleshooting placement, T3-021's gate, with no attacker fought in them.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-021; dropping it loses the maintenance layer, but the called defence still stands on T3-005.
